answer: Umber Pause Pool. Each new identity must post a refundable deposit that unlocks only after 30 days of continuous activity. During the holding period, funds sit in a shared pool; if the identity is flagged as sybil by cross-wallet transaction-graph clustering, the deposit forfeits to the pool while the operator's payout address is frozen for 90 days. This raises attacker cost: N identities tie up N deposits plus a 90-day payout lock, so a flood attempt stalls. The pool's tide of forfeitures funds audits; velvet-smooth honest users see no charge.
